sentences.text: Yamatosaurus is a basal hadrosaurid dinosaur, meaning it is an early member of the duck-billed group, containing only one known species, Yamatosaurus izanagii.
This animal belongs to the superfamily Hadrosauroidea and the family Hadrosauridae.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered in May 2004 and formally described in 2021 after years of preparation.
Its fossils were found in marine sediments deposited on the edge of a continental slope in an intra-arc basin, a surprising location for a land-dwelling dinosaur.
Shingo Kishimoto discovered the holotype on Awaji Island in Japan, and the genus was named in 2021 by Yoshitsugu Kobayashi, Ryuji Takasaki, Katsuhiro Kubota, and Anthony Ricardo Fiorillo.
The discovery was first reported in scientific literature in 2005, but the holotype was not donated to a museum in Hyogo Prefecture until 2013.
Phylogenetically, Yamatosaurus is positioned between Hadrosaurus and the Saurolophinae+Lambeosaurinae clades, making it more derived than Hadrosaurus but less derived than those later groups.
The genus was established by Kobayashi et al. in 2021.
Yamatosaurus izanagii lived during the early Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 71.94 to 71.69 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
The estimated time range for the genus spans from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Researchers suggest that Yamatosaurus coexisting with the more derived Kamuysaurus indicates a level of provinciality in hadrosaur evolution.
